title: Shortfall Paydown Amount on Operating Lines of Credit
content:
The amount of a paydown that brings one of the Operating Lines of Credit back within its borrowing base is the line's outstanding principal less its lendable limit.

## Definitions

- **Lendable limit**: the lower of the commitment and the borrowing base on the line's most recent certificate when the product requires a borrowing base, and the commitment when it does not.
- **Outstanding principal**: the principal worked out from the line's transaction history — advances plus returned principal payments less principal payments.
- **Paydown**: the outstanding principal less the lendable limit, never less than zero, rounded to cents.

The borrowing base used is the one standing on the line's certificate with the latest as-of date.

## Worked figure (hypothetical Borrowing Base Operating Line)

| Item | Figure |
|---|---|
| Commitment | USD 2,000,000.00 |
| Borrowing base on the most recent certificate | USD 1,400,000.00 |
| Lendable limit — the lower of the two | USD 1,400,000.00 |
| Advances on the line | USD 1,823,456.78 |
| Returned principal payments | USD 25,000.00 |
| Principal payments | USD 325,000.00 |
| Outstanding principal | USD 1,823,456.78 plus USD 25,000.00 less USD 325,000.00, that is USD 1,523,456.78 |
| Paydown | USD 1,523,456.78 less USD 1,400,000.00, that is USD 123,456.78 |

## Points of judgement

- With the same history and a borrowing base of USD 1,600,000.00 on the most recent certificate, the outstanding principal is below the lendable limit and the paydown is zero.
- With a borrowing base above the commitment, the commitment is the lendable limit.
